data.title: Nvidia's share slide knocks it below Alphabet in valuation
data.description: Nov 20 : Nvidia, the centerpiece of Wall Street's AI trade, slipped behind Google parent Alphabet to become the fourth-most valuable US company on Friday, as a prolonged selloff in the chipmaker's shares reshuffled the top of the market-value rankings. The stock, last down 3 per cent and valued at $3.4 trillion, was on course for a seventh straight weekly decline, its longest losing streak since 2008. The slide comes days after Nvidia's first earnings report since co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation, which failed to ease investor concerns about leadership and the durability of AI spending. Nvidia's fall down the market-value rankings also underscores a shift within the AI trade, as investors gravitate toward companies that pair heavy AI investment with established cloud and software revenue streams. Apple, seen as less exposed to the AI trade, remained well ahead with a market value of $5.08 trillion. Microsoft ranked second at $3.72 trillion, followed by Alphabet at $3.44 trillion, according to LSEG data.

data.title: UK finds fix for fridge and freezer vulnerability after European hacks
data.description: LONDON, Nov 20 : A British cybersecurity operation has fixed a flaw in the operating systems of commercial fridges and freezers used by supermarkets, warehouses and restaurants, helping protect them from hacks that hit several European countries in recent weeks. A wave of cyberattacks knocked out commercial fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium earlier in November, while a similar hack hit France in October, forcing stores to throw away millions of euros' worth of food. It was thought Britain had largely escaped the hacks because its refrigeration industry relies on different devices, but those working with retailers found a flaw that could have provided an opening for hackers. "We were aware of a small number of UK organisations that may have been affected as a result of vulnerabilities on their systems, and the National Cyber Security Centre immediately took steps to alert and support those that could have been impacted," an NCSC spokesperson said. Following the attacks in Europe, Germany's information security office warned of continuing vulnerabilities in some of Danish firm Danfoss' industrial cooling appliances. French intelligence and cyber agencies accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of carrying out the October hack, which targeted 700 commercial sites and caused 15 fires after hackers raised temperatures in refrigeration systems. The vulnerability affecting British refrigeration systems was identified by consultants at Omega Systems, before ethical hackers from cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners found a series of additional openings and contacted security services. Pen Test Partners said the operation lasted for about three weeks and was carried out in secret so as not to alert hackers. Before the fix could be made, the affected companies removed fridges from the open internet and prioritised efforts to secure the devices. The NCSC said it shared security advice with food and retail organisations to ensure they took measures to mitigate the risks.

data.title: Bertelsmann rules out gaming push despite GTA VI frenzy, CEO says
data.description: Nov 19 : Bertelsmann has no plan to enter the video games market despite the blockbuster success of "Grand Theft Auto VI," said Thomas Rabe, CEO of the German media group that published the original game in the franchise. Huge global demand for GTA VI is expected to generate revenue far exceeding its estimated development costs of around $1 billion. But "not every game becomes as successful as GTA," Rabe said and cautioned that gaming remains a hit-driven business, similar to the film industry. "New games are not easy to establish." Bertelsmann's BMG Interactive division published the first "Grand Theft Auto" in 1997. The next year, the company sold the business to Take-Two Interactive, which went on to develop one of the world's most successful gaming franchises. Rabe said his company has repeatedly examined entering the gaming market over the past 10 to 15 years, but decided against it. He cited high acquisition costs, reputational risks and the industry's reliance on a few blockbusters. Bertelsmann, whose businesses include broadcaster RTL Group, publisher Penguin Random House, music company BMG and logistics provider Arvato, sees little need to expand into other sectors, Rabe said.

data.title: Italy gives green light to Tesla self-driving system ahead of EU approval
data.description: ROME, Nov 20 : Italy has given provisional approval to Tesla's Assisted Driving System (TAD), Transport Minister Matteo Salvini said on Friday, making it the first major European Union country to embrace the technology developed by the U.S. electric vehicle maker. In a post on X, Salvini said the decision was "another step forward toward innovation, technology and the mobility of the future". The green light followed "a thorough technical feasibility assessment", the minister said, and came ahead of an ongoing European Union approval process. Tesla's CEO Elon Musk wrote back on X: "Thank you, much appreciated!" TAD, formerly known as Full Self-Driving (FSD), is a so-called 'hands-off, eyes-on' system, that allows a vehicle to drive autonomously while requiring continuous supervision from a behind the steering-wheel. Several smaller EU countries have already taken the same step as Italy. After receiving initial approval in the Netherlands in April, the system was subsequently recognised in countries including Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, and Belgium, allowing Tesla to expand its footprint ahead of a broader EU vote. Tesla also said on X on Friday that TAD had been approved in Italy, posting a video from inside one of its cars navigating the streets of Rome in autonomous mode.

data.title: Chile, Japan to boost cooperation on critical minerals, Chile's Kast says
data.description: SANTIAGO, Nov 20 : Chile will seek to strengthen cooperation with Japan on critical minerals to ensure resilience and stability in supply chains, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast said on Friday. • "We are committed to strengthening cooperation on critical minerals, including copper," Kast said after meeting Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during an official visit to Japan • Chile is the world's largest copper producer and second-largest lithium producer. Both metals are key to electric vehicles and battery energy storage systems • The cooperation will "contribute to the resilience and stability of global supply chains by ensuring that trade measures are consistent with relevant international agreements", a joint statement added • Kast and Takaichi cited a project at Chilean state-run Codelco's El Teniente copper mine as a concrete example of their cooperation • In August, the mine began testing a next-generation photonics communication network developed in Japan • They also backed a free international economic order and signed a memorandum of cooperation on information and communication technologies

data.title: Trump says US to penalize firms building data centers abroad
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the US would penalize American companies that build data centers overseas.  "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said while discussing AI at a White House news conference following his trip to Asia. He said he would impose a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers abroad. Data centers are critical to the AI boom because they provide the computing power needed to train and run increasingly complex AI systems, and a penalty could complicate the global AI buildout. Data center developers often locate facilities close to users to reduce delays for time-sensitive tasks such as payment processing. Transmitting large volumes of data over long distances can also add significant costs.

data.title: Mercedes gets German approval for assisted point-to-point driving
data.description: Nov 20 : Mercedes-Benz said on Friday it had become the first automaker to receive regulatory approval for assisted point-to-point driving in Germany, a milestone in the race to deploy more advanced automated-driving systems on public roads. It will launch an early-access programme in Stuttgart and Munich in late 2026, ahead of a broader German rollout in the first half of 2027. A harmonised regulatory framework expected to take effect in January 2027 could also enable expansion to other markets covered by UN Regulation R171, it said.

data.title: Saudi Arabia once banned Grand Theft Auto. Now it's got a stake in it
data.description: Nov 20 : Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being embraced not only by its gamers - a category that includes Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman - but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs. This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon launch — the first new release of the top-selling series since a Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025. "Playing GTA VI in Saudi Arabia legally makes me so happy, because we're talking about a game that was banned," local content creator Thamer al Dairem said from a windowless, air-conditioned room, lit mostly by the bank of monitors displaying the game. "We're talking about the biggest game in the world." Support and investment in gaming by Saudi Arabia have been rising fast, not least from de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, often known by his initials MBS, who told Fox News in 2023 that gaming helped him disconnect and let off steam. The Public Investment Fund (PIF), the sovereign wealth fund he chairs, owns a major stake worth over $2 billion in Take-Two Interactive, the US firm that owns Grand Theft Auto-developer Rockstar Games, LSEG Workspace data show. CHANGING CUSTOMS IN CONSERVATIVE SAUDI ARABIA In August, a consortium including PIF acquired gaming giant Electronic Arts for $55 billion. This month, gaming software provider Unity Software held talks with investors including the Saudi sovereign wealth fund on a potential buyout valuing it at around $25 billion. PIF, which has spent the past year consolidating its gaming holdings into a subsidiary, Savvy Games Group, declined to comment. MBS has been leading a campaign to open Saudi Arabia up and ease strict social and cultural norms that revolve around a conservative interpretation of Islam — a far cry from GTA VI's Vice City. GTA VI advertisements have been appearing in some of Saudi Arabia's most popular shopping malls. One image shows the heroine wearing shorts and a crop top, her arm resting on her partner's shoulder — unthinkable a few years ago, when women were required to dress modestly and cover their hair. MBS's wider reform plan, dubbed Vision 2030, is all about reducing reliance on oil and gas revenues, both in the economy and in state revenues, and PIF strategy is part of that. "(It) is part of a diversified long-term investment strategy to capture value from industries it does not traditionally operate within," said Piers Harding-Rolls, who researches games at Ampere Analysis. In Riyadh, al Dairem is now streaming Grand Theft Auto content and says that, while some of the depictions of violence, drugs and sex are extreme, the game is age-restricted and reflects another country. "The city is Vice City, and it's representing Miami and the chaotic things that happen. For us Saudis, like, we know that it has nothing to do with us." The gaming experience, on the other hand, matters hugely to him. "When I saw the ads of GTA VI in the malls, I was so happy. If you'd asked me if I was ever going to see this, like, 10 years ago in Saudi, I wouldn't have believed it." (Editing by Adam Jourdan and Kevin Liffey)

data.title: PayPal taps Xero's Claire Bramley as CFO, succeeding Jamie Miller
data.description: Nov 20 : PayPal named Xero's Claire Bramley as chief financial officer on Friday, succeeding Jamie Miller, in a broader shake-up of its senior leadership team as the payments firm pursues an ambitious turnaround. Once a pandemic-era darling, PayPal has lost ground as consumers increasingly turn to payment services embedded in their smartphones, leaving its shares well below the record highs reached in 2021. The shift has been amplified by the expansion of Big Tech into digital payments through services such as Google Pay and Apple Pay, chipping away at PayPal's market share and dampening investor confidence. Bramley is set to join PayPal on February 1 from Xero, a global small-business platform, where she has served as CFO since April 2025. "Notable leadership changes add another layer of complexity to PYPL's turnaround, with more organization disruption likely before potential benefits emerge," TD Cowen analysts wrote in a note. "Thus, 2027 is set to be another transition year." PayPal shares were last down 3 per cent in morning trading. In her new role, Bramley will be tasked with advancing the company's multi-year plan to streamline operations, cut costs and improve margins. PayPal has set a goal of securing at least $1.5 billion in gross run-rate savings over the next two to three years. The company has also tapped American Express' Kartik Mani as president and head of consumer financial services and Venmo — its flagship peer-to-peer payments platform. Juan Rio is set to join PayPal from Brightstar.AI as executive vice-president of AI business transformation and operations at the end of November. Accelerating AI adoption through the integration of AI and automation across PayPal's business accounts for about 40 per cent of its savings target. PayPal currently has a market value of roughly $47 billion, versus its peak of about $360 billion in 2021.

data.title: Apollo, Goldman lead $44 billion SpaceX GPU debt financing
data.description: Nov 20 : Apollo and Goldman Sachs said on Friday they priced about $44 billion of senior and subordinated notes to fund the purchase of GPUs and related equipment for SpaceX , in what the firms called the largest GPU financing to date. The deal underscores the large capital requirements of the AI boom as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out computing infrastructure needed to support AI development. Here are more details: • The transaction, which was oversubscribed and upsized because of strong investor demand, is expected to finance the next generation of Nvidia Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout. • Lease schedules are expected to start when the GPUs and related equipment are delivered in the first half of 2027 • BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and accounts advised by KKR provided anchor commitments • SpaceX said last month that an affiliate of Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the company in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion

data.title: Anthropic's IPO bank closed position meant to stabilize stock, removing source of support
data.description: Nov 20 : Anthropic's underwriter, tasked with stabilizing its share price after its market debut, closed a position meant to do that, Anthropic said on Friday. With the AI company's shares falling 11 per cent, the move means one potential source of buying support is now unavailable.  Anthropic named investment bank Morgan Stanley as the initial public offering's stabilization agent to support the stock after its market debut. In that role, the bank received an option, known as a greenshoe, to buy additional shares — 147 million in Anthropic’s case — directly from the company on behalf of the underwriting syndicate.  Alternatively, the underwriters can buy shares in the open market to cover the greenshoe, which can support the stock price. In the case of Anthropic, whose shares closed on Thursday at $97.17, about 17 per cent above its IPO price, Morgan Stanley exercised the full greenshoe at the IPO price, Anthropic said. The stock was last down 11.5 per cent on Friday at $86, after falling to as low as $85 earlier in the session. The exercise brought aggregate gross proceeds from the IPO to roughly $93.5 billion. Underwriters typically have up to 30 days after an IPO to exercise the greenshoe option, which allows them to buy additional shares directly from the company to cover shares sold in excess of the original offering. It is common for underwriters to exercise the greenshoe when shares are trading above their IPO price on the first day of trading, as they can buy the additional shares directly from the company at the offering price. With the full option exercised, Morgan Stanley can no longer use open-market purchases to cover any remaining overallotment if shares fall below the $83 IPO price. Market participants have questioned the underwriters' timing given Thursday's market volatility, one person familiar with the matter said. Morgan Stanley declined to comment. Carsten Hesse, London-based head of index events at Berenberg, said the development is positive for Anthropic as it increases the proceeds raised in the IPO."However, it is less positive for investors, who are losing an important potential source of buying support," he said in a note to clients. "It seems like the bookrunners have given up their remaining stabilisation option already after 1 day just as the share price is getting closer to the IPO price." Anthropic’s IPO roadshow and strong market debut raised hopes that other AI companies could follow it to the public markets, with issuers looking to capitalize on renewed investor appetite. SB Energy, a company that develops, owns and operates data centers and power infrastructure, updated its IPO prospectus with the latest financial information shortly after Anthropic priced its offering, underscoring how companies were preparing to move ahead. But that optimism was tested late on Thursday as a broader selloff in technology stocks gathered pace.

data.title: OakNorth wins US banking licence
data.description: LONDON, Nov 20 : British-based digital bank OakNorth has secured a US banking charter, it said on Friday, the first such foreign online lender to win a broader banking licence in the world's biggest economy as it seeks to grow income. OakNorth, which is backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners as well as Japan's SoftBank, will now be able to expand beyond lending to provide basic services such as checking and savings accounts. The development shows how digital banks are increasingly diversifying worldwide as they seek to disrupt bricks-and-mortar incumbents, leaning on their lower cost base and more modern technology to win business from traditional lenders. • OakNorth has bought Community Unity Bank in Michigan, it said on Friday, allowing it to provide a wider range of services as it builds its US business • The bank will hire tens of staff in the US as it grows the business, CEO Rishi Khosla told Reuters in an interview • OakNorth is targeting lower middle-market businesses with revenue of $5 million to $100 million, Khosla said • "We can deliver speed, reliability, and consistency for our customers, which enables us to win against community banks, regional banks and the like," Khosla said.

data.title: Anthropic IPO haul rises to $93.5 billion after underwriters exercise greenshoe
data.description: Nov 20 : Anthropic said on Friday that its underwriters had exercised the "greenshoe" option to purchase additional shares, increasing ​the total proceeds from its initial public offering to roughly $93.5 billion.

data.title: Anthropic founder to make large gift to Trump accounts, Bessent says
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 20 : A founder of the artificial intelligence giant Anthropic will make a large gift to cradle-to-adulthood investment ​program, Trump Accounts, in the coming weeks, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with CNBC on Friday. Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its blockbuster IPO on Thursday after underwriters exercised an option to ​buy additional shares "One of the Anthropic founders is going to make a large gift to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks," Bessent said. "We believe that it's important for these great entrepreneurs to share their bounty." Trump Accounts, which will provide U.S. citizens born between 2025 and 2028 ‌a government-funded investment account of $1,000 that families can build on, is aimed at promoting investing and financial literacy from an early age.

data.title: Alphabet raises $4.19 billion in Canadian bond offering
data.description: Nov 20 : Alphabet has raised C$6 billion ($4.19 billion) through a four-tranche Canadian bond offering, according to a pricing term sheet filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. Big technology companies are increasingly tapping debt markets and ​raising equity ⁠to bolster AI infrastructure, marking a shift from their traditional reliance on cash to fund investments. The money raised would be used for general corporate purposes, which could include repayment of outstanding debt, the Google parent said in the filing. Alphabet expects to receive about C$5.97 billion after underwriting discounts, or bank fees, and before expenses. The offering was priced on November 19 and is scheduled to settle on November 24. The notes are senior unsecured debt and have received a rating of Aa2 with a "stable" outlook from Moody's, and AA+ with a "stable" outlook from S&P, the filing showed. RBC Dominion Securities, Scotia Capital and TD Securities are joint book-running managers for the transaction, while CIBC World Markets is a co-manager. Big Tech rival Meta in October announced plans for its largest-ever equity offerings of around $97.5 billion, including stock sales of about $37.5 billion, and plans to later raise up to $60 billion through an at-the-market share-sale program, or a plan to sell shares into the market over time at prevailing prices. Alphabet had increased its equity offerings to $84.75 billion in June. Last month, the company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, versus analysts' expectation that it would come close to breaking even. ($1 = 1.4322 Canadian dollars)
